The victim is an American citizen, according to Valley News Live.Calzada-Becerril and Amoles made their first court appearance on Friday, November 6. Both have been charged with kidnapping, along with additional counts including domestic violence and assault, Valley News Live reported.A judge set bail at $500,000 each. Prosecutors said both defendants could face deportation. Additional charges may be filed as the investigation continues.According to court documents, Amoles was usually responsible for handling the victim and unlocking her from the bedframe. She returned to the apartment with her eight-year-old daughter shortly after authorities discovered the woman.Residents of the apartment complex said they were stunned to learn that a woman had allegedly been held captive in the building for two years without their knowledge.Erin Schauer, a resident, told Valley News Live that security personnel regularly patrolled the complex."We have security coming through from like 6 to 11 p.m. every single night. They stop in the hallways, they walk through every single building, they drive around," she said."That is really scary. You hear about that all the time on the news, but the fact that it was literally right over there," she added.Another resident, Reed Bertsch, said he could not understand how nobody had suspected what was happening."It's unbelievable. I just can't believe no one heard it, or you know, had any suspicion of something like that going on," he said.A longtime tenant also told Valley News Live that she had noticed the foil covering the apartment windows for years but had not known why it was there.Fargo police are working with the Cass County State's Attorney's Office as the case proceeds, according to Valley News Live.
Article Summary: Woman was found after maintenance worker heard her cries for help. She was restrained by a heavy chain and padlock around her right ankle. Ex-husband Arturo Calzada-Becerril, 40, and his girlfriend, Erendira Amoles, 41, have been charged in connection with the case.

Article Title: In 1883, Harriet Strong was left with four daughters and a debt-ridden ranch after her husband’s death; she later developed water-storage systems that anticipated major US projects
Article Text:
PC: USPTO

How Harriet Strong inherited a debt-ridden ranch in 1883

How walnut farming and pampas grass helped her rebuild the business

How a walnut orchard inspired Harriet Strong's water inventions

The 1893 Chicago World's Fair brought wider recognition

How Harriet Strong expanded her work beyond agriculture

Her Colorado River proposal reached Congress during World War I

Hoover Dam and the All-American Canal followed years later

In 1883, Harriet Williams Russell Strong found herself responsible for a struggling California ranch, four young daughters and debts left behind by her late husband. She had little experience managing agricultural land and was still dealing with persistent health problems. The ranch, however, depended on something she soon began to understand better than most experienced farmers: water. As she worked to keep the property financially viable, Strong developed ways to store and control water for irrigation, eventually securing several US patents. Her work took her beyond farming and into public policy, where she argued for large-scale water management projects that would influence the development of the American West.Harriet Strong's circumstances changed dramatically in 1883 when her husband, Charles Strong, died by suicide following the collapse of another business venture. He had lost money in a mining investment that turned out to be worthless, leaving Harriet to deal with the financial consequences. At the time, she was in Philadelphia receiving treatment for a longstanding spinal condition. Her four daughters, aged between 10 and 14, were living in Whittier, California.According to the United States Patent and Trademark Office (USPTO), after completing her treatment, Harriet returned to California and took responsibility for the family's 220-acre Rancho del Fuerte. The property was facing financial difficulties, and creditors were seeking to recover the money owed by her late husband. She had no formal agricultural training and was not in particularly good health, but losing the ranch was not an option she was prepared to accept.She began studying farming through books, scientific publications and conversations with neighbouring landowners. Her research covered everything from soil conditions and crop selection to irrigation and agricultural markets.Strong identified walnuts as a potentially profitable crop and devoted around 150 acres of the property to growing walnut trees. There was a practical difficulty, though. The trees needed substantial quantities of water and took years to produce a commercial harvest. She needed another source of income while waiting for the orchard to mature.As reported by USPTO), her solution was Argentine pampas grass, a fast-growing plant that could be cultivated between the rows of walnut trees. Its decorative plumes were increasingly popular during the Victorian period, particularly as alternatives to feathers used in fashionable hats. Strong recognised that the crop could provide an additional income stream without requiring her to abandon the long-term walnut plan.Pampas plumes sold wholesale for around four cents each, a considerable sum for the period, and Strong found ways to keep the business going as consumer tastes changed. She supplied coloured red, white and blue plumes for the 1892 and 1896 Democratic and Republican national conventions, turning the decorative grass into a product with a market beyond ordinary household and fashion use.The success of the walnut orchard depended heavily on reliable irrigation. Southern California's climate presented a difficult combination of limited rainfall and sudden, destructive floods. Heavy storms could send large volumes of water through the Los Angeles basin, damaging farmland and carrying away resources that might otherwise have been stored for dry periods.Strong began working on ways to address both problems. Instead of allowing stormwater to run off the land, she developed a system of reservoirs and interconnected dams designed to retain water for agricultural use. Her approach involved a series of ascending dams, with each structure helping to support the one above it.Beginning in 1887, Strong secured patents covering dam and reservoir construction and irrigation systems. She eventually became the named inventor on five US patents.Strong's business success gave her an opportunity to present her agricultural and inventive work to a national audience. At the 1893 World's Columbian Exposition in Chicago, she received two medals for her inventions and promoted the products grown on her ranch.One of the most unusual displays associated with her visit was the Pampas Plume Palace, an elaborate structure made largely from the grass she cultivated. Her daughters helped with its construction. The display attracted attention at a time when decorative pampas plumes were a fashionable commercial product.The fair also gave Strong a platform to discuss women's participation in business. She spoke at a congress devoted to business training for women, arguing that practical knowledge of commercial affairs could help women take a greater role in public administration.By the early 20th century, Strong's interests had expanded well beyond her ranch. Her knowledge of water management brought her into discussions about flood prevention and the infrastructure needed to support agriculture across Southern California.She played a part in the campaign that led to the Los Angeles Flood Control Act of 1915 and served on a flood control board. Her public involvement came at a time when women in the United States were still fighting for basic political representation. California had granted women the right to vote in 1911, but Strong's participation in public affairs had begun before that change.In 1918, she became the first woman delegate to attend a convention of the US Chamber of Commerce, another indication of how far her career had moved from the management of a single agricultural property.During the First World War, Strong travelled to Washington, DC, to present Congress with a proposal for a major dam on the Colorado River, near the lower end of the Grand Canyon. Her plan was intended to achieve several objectives at once: regulate flooding, conserve water, generate hydroelectric power and provide irrigation to farmland.The agricultural argument was particularly relevant during wartime. Strong believed that a dependable water supply could increase food production in the American West, helping the United States support Allied forces and civilians affected by the conflict.She viewed the Colorado River as a resource that needed to be managed on a regional scale rather than through isolated agricultural projects. Her proposal anticipated the role that large dams and canal networks would later play in supplying water to farms and settlements across the region.Congress did not approve her plan as the war came to an end. Strong believed the proposal had been dismissed partly because it had come from a woman rather than because of its practical merits.Harriet Strong died in a car accident in 1926, before the large Colorado River projects she had advocated for became reality. Her ideas, however, remained relevant as the federal government moved towards developing major water infrastructure in the region.Congress approved the Boulder Canyon Project in 1928, providing the legislative foundation for the construction of Hoover Dam. Work on the structure was completed in 1935. The dam became a major source of hydroelectric power while helping regulate the Colorado River and store water for use across the Southwest.The legislation also provided for the All-American Canal, a major irrigation project intended to carry Colorado River water into California's Imperial Valley. Construction began in 1942, and the canal became a central part of the region's agricultural water supply.
Article Summary: Harriet Williams Russell Strong inherited a debt-ridden ranch in 1883. She developed ways to store and control water for irrigation. Her work took her beyond farming and into public policy. She argued for large-scale water management projects that would influence the development of the American West.

Article Title: 'Deport all dot heads': Far-right activist Jake Lang targets Hindus at Seattle Diwali event
Article Text:
Far-right activist Jake Lang disrupts Seattle Diwali celebrations with anti-Hindu placards

A Diwali celebration in Seattle was disrupted on Saturday (local time) after far-right American activist Jake Lang and a group of protesters attempted to interrupt the festivities while carrying placards reading "Deport All Dot Heads". Lang was confronted and physically stopped by some of the people present at the event.Following the incident, Lang posted pictures of the attempted disruption on X and launched an abusive tirade against Hindus, accusing them of being responsible for turning Texas blue in favour of the Democrats.US Congresswoman Pramila Jayapal and other prominent Indian Americans have condemned the disruption.In a post on X, Jayapal expressed outrage over the incident, describing it as a racist display and saying the Indian-American community should be able to celebrate the festival without fear."I am beyond disgusted by this vile and racist display. Diwali is an important holiday and our community should feel safe to celebrate it. This hateful display has no place in our city or this country," she wrote.Indian-American businessman Ajay Jain Bhutoria also condemned the incident, calling it "pure bigotry" and saying racial slurs targeting Hindus had no place in the United States."Absolutely disgusting. Jake Lang and Thomas Allen storming a peaceful Diwali celebration in Seattle with signs reading “Deport All Dot Heads” and “Stop Hindu Replacement of Christians” is pure hate and bigotry.Diwali is a festival of light, family, and joy — not a threat. Targeting Hindu Americans and Indian immigrants with racial slurs and conspiracy rhetoric has no place in this country. We stand against this racism and for the right of every American to celebrate their heritage freely. #StopAsianHate," he said in a post on X.The Coalition of Hindus of North America (CoHNA) also condemned the disruption and urged community members in Seattle and surrounding areas to remain vigilant, warning that the activists had announced plans to disrupt other Diwali celebrations.In a post on X, the organisation said, "Community Alert for Seattle and surrounding areas! Hinduphobic bigotry on open display as activists Jake Lang and Thomas Allen burst in to disrupt a Hindu Diwali celebration where children are performing, holding signs such as “Deport all Dotheads” and “Stop Hindu Replacement of Christians”. Thankfully, there were others who didn’t tolerate this and removed them from the premises. We condemn such actions and advise community members to stay vigilant while celebrating Diwali, as these activists have announced plans to disrupt other celebrations."Lang heads an organisation called White Replacement and was among those who participated in the January 6, 2021, attack on the US Capitol. He served four years in prison before being pardoned by US President Donald Trump on the first day of his second presidency in 2025.The incident came shortly after Trump celebrated Diwali at the White House with Indian tech entrepreneur Vishal Gondal, chef Vikas Mehta and others at the Oval Office. The US President participated in a ceremonial diya-lighting and was presented with a copy of the Hanuman Chalisa.Meanwhile, Washington State Governor Bob Ferguson also marked the festival at the state's Legislative Building in Olympia, alongside the Consul General of India and state Senator Manka Dhingra.In a post on X, Ferguson said, "We had an incredible celebration of Diwali inside the Legislative Building this week with the Consulate General of India and Sen. Dhingra, and I proclaimed this Sunday to be Diwali, The Festival of Lights In Washington State. Washington state is proud to be home to one of the largest communities of Indian Americans in the country. During the previous decade, we had the fastest growing Indian American population in the entire country. And we have seen this community contribute so much to our state."The attempted disruption in Seattle also comes days after another right-wing activist allegedly plotted a mass shooting at a Hindu temple near Chicago. A 19-year-old suspect, identified as Alexandros Paporakis, was arrested following an investigation into threats against the temple. The suspect, who professed Nazi ideology, had allegedly outlined a plan to carry out an attack.Meanwhile, Lang has also claimed that the US midterm election results, which saw Democrats make gains in states such as Texas and Kansas, were rigged. Calling for a protest ahead of the anniversary of the January 6 Capitol attack, he said, "On January 3rd 2027, Christian Crusaders will descend upon the US Capitol in Washington DC to PROTEST the Certification of the RIGGED Midterms!!!!"Texas saw Democratic victories in the Senate and gubernatorial races, with James Talarico winning the Senate seat and Gina Hinojosa becoming governor.
Article Summary: Far-right activist Jake Lang disrupts Seattle Diwali celebrations with anti- Hindu placards. US Congresswoman Pramila Jayapal and other prominent Indian Americans have condemned the disruption. Incident comes days after another right-wing activist allegedly plotted a mass shooting at a Hindu temple near Chicago.

Article Title: In 2025, a Virginia grandmother won $150,000 in the Powerball after asking ChatGPT for lottery numbers, then donated the entire prize to three charities close to her heart
Article Text:
Image: Virginia Lottery

How a friend’s lottery advice, an online ticket and ChatGPT led to a Powerball win

Why she decided within moments that the windfall was not hers to keep and where it should go

How a naval family’s legacy sent money to military households as government pay worries grew

The husband’s illness behind a gift to dementia research and what the money was meant to fund

Why a food-growing organisation near Richmond saw her gift arrive just as demand surged

In 2025, Carrie Edwards of Midlothian won the prize and gave every dollar of it to three charities. Her story spread around the world after the Virginia Lottery publicised the gift. A retired public relations professional who rarely played, she says the decision to give the prize away came to her instantly. The causes she chose reflect her father’s naval career, her late husband’s illness and her volunteer work with a food-growing organisation in the Richmond area, and two of them received the money as demand for their services rose.According to The Washington Post, Edwards, who was 68 when the story was reported, walked into a 7-Eleven with a friend who wanted two Powerball tickets. The jackpot for the 6 September 2025 drawing had climbed above $1.7 billion, the second-largest ever. Edwards hardly ever played, and her friend, an active player, gave her two warnings, always buy a paper ticket, and never touch the Powerball multiplier because it is a scam. She ignored both.Instead, she created a Virginia Lottery account on her phone. Rather than relying on family birthdays or lucky numbers, she asked ChatGPT, which she had only recently started using for research, whether it had any winning numbers for her.The chatbot first replied that luck is luck, then supplied a set of numbers. She entered them and paid an extra dollar for the Power Play option.When she missed the huge jackpot, she assumed luck had not been on her side. She had not realised that she had chosen the option that re-enters the same numbers in the next drawing. A phone notification told her she had won, and she suspected a scam or a small prize of perhaps $10. Out of curiosity, she logged in and found she had matched four of the five numbers plus the Powerball, a $50,000 prize that the multiplier tripled.Alone in her kitchen, Edwards was thunderstruck by the news. Almost at once, she said, she felt an overpowering conviction that the money was not hers. She resolved to give it all to her three most cherished charities.Her next thought was a joke at the expense of the friend whose advice she had ignored. He is an Army veteran, while she comes from a Navy family, so she privately gave the Navy the first point. Her three adult children were surprised by the win, and they supported her decision.Edwards is the daughter of a career naval officer. Her late father, a fighter pilot who ended his career in the office of the chief of naval operations at the Pentagon, asked in his will that his children donate part of their inheritance to the Navy-Marine Corps Relief Society. The non-profit provides financial assistance and other services to members of the military and their families.Her gift reached the society at a critical moment, according to its president and chief executive, Robert Ruark. Concerns were growing over government pay and furloughs as the federal government shut down at the end of September 2025. Ruark said the money was being used to help families facing hardship from the shutdown, deployments and everyday family emergencies.Her late husband, Steve, inspired the second donation. In his late 50s, he was diagnosed with frontotemporal degeneration, the most common form of dementia in people under 60, which has no approved treatment to stop or slow it. As his condition worsened, Edwards retired from her public relations work to care for him. In 2023, the couple moved from Fairfax County in Northern Virginia to Midlothian, a Richmond suburb, so he could be closer to their children and new grandchildren. Steve died at the end of that year.After retiring, Edwards began volunteering for and giving to the Association for Frontotemporal Degeneration. Its chief executive, Susan Dickinson, said gifts range from $5 to more than $1 million, but the larger sums usually come from research partnerships and benefactors, so a single donation of Edwards’s size is rare. Dickinson described it as wonderfully impactful. The money was to go towards research, grants for pilot programmes, and bringing together people with the disease and those working on treatments.The third beneficiary was Shalom Farms, where Edwards volunteered and served on the board when the story was reported. The non-profit grows fresh local produce and distributes it to about 10,000 Richmond residents. Her gift landed when the shutdown delayed food-assistance benefits, which drove a surge in demand.Executive Director Anna Ibrahim said the surprise donation let the farm buy more items so that it would have enough for everyone who came. The money was also to be invested across the organisation to support local farmers and other initiatives.Edwards told The Washington Post she had no regrets. She felt blessed to have been able to spread the word about causes she holds dear, and she hoped to inspire others. The attention, she said, gave her a platform to set an example for her children and to honour her husband’s and her father’s legacies through actions rather than words.
Article Summary: Carrie Edwards, 68, of Midlothian, Virginia, won the prize in 2025. She gave every dollar of it to three charities. The causes reflect her father's naval career, her late husband’s illness and her volunteer work with a food-growing organisation.

Article Title: NBA star Chris Paul backed Sour Patch Kids’ $1 million HBCU scholarship programme, with 10 students eligible to receive up to $16,700 each
Article Text:
PC: Wikipedia

Sour Patch Kids commits $1 million to HBCU scholarships with Chris Paul

Mischief for Change Scholarship offered 10 awards of up to $16,700

NBA star Chris Paul joined students to announce scholarship opportunity

What financial challenges were HBCU and PBI students facing

Sour Patch Kids partnered with the Thurgood Marshall College Fund (TMCF) and received support from basketball star Chris Paul for a scholarship initiative backed by a $1 million commitment over five years. The programme, called the Mischief for Change Scholarship, aimed to provide financial assistance to students attending Historically Black Colleges and Universities (HBCUs) and Predominantly Black Institutions (PBIs). Chris Paul joined the team as a judge, helping select the recipients. The initiative invited current and incoming students to apply for financial support. According to Thurgood Marshall College Fund(2021), the partnership offered scholarships to students enrolled at one of its member schools. The fund shared application details online through its official website.The Sour Patch Kids brand partnered with TMCF to offer financial assistance to students attending one of the fund’s member schools. The initiative was called the Mischief for Change Scholarship and formed part of the brand’s $1 million commitment over five years. The fund was intended to support scholarships for students attending HBCUs and PBIs.The announcement invited current and incoming students of these institutions to apply.Chris Paul joined the team as a judge and helped select the scholarship recipients. The partnership brought together the brand, the college fund and the basketball star for a programme focused on student financial assistance.The scholarship offered 10 awards, with each valued at up to $16,700. The amount could be paid as $8,350 per semester. The programme was open to current and incoming students attending an HBCU or PBI that was a TMCF member school. Chris Paul joined the selection team as a judge. The announcement said that 10 scholars would be selected with his help. The scholarship was presented as a way to provide financial assistance to students pursuing their education at the eligible institutions.Chris Paul helped introduce the scholarship by joining a virtual meeting with a group of students in the Phoenix area. He announced the scholarship. Paul said, “As an active proponent of HBCUs, I’m honored to help SOUR PATCH KIDS and TMCF select the recipients of this year’s Mischief for Change Scholarship.”“I’ve seen firsthand the impact a HBCU education can have on students and our communities. I’m excited to share this opportunity and can’t wait to see how these future leaders shape our world.”TMCF President and Chief Executive Officer Dr Harry L. Williams said, “Today’s college bound students are facing incredible challenges, with students attending HBCUs and PBIs leaving with more debt than ever before.”“Our HBCU scholars are current and future changemakers of our society and our hope is that the Mischief for Change Scholarship can provide those incredible students with the financial assistance they need to focus on what matters most.”Sour Patch Kids Associate Director of Marketing Mili Laddha said, “The SOUR PATCH KIDS brand is well-known for its loveably mischievous mascots – the Kids.”“Through the Mischief for Change Scholarship, we’re recognizing playful students who are creatively diffusing tension, challenging perceptions and sparking meaningful dialogue.”
Article Summary: Sour Patch Kids partnered with Thurgood Marshall College Fund (TMCF) and basketball star Chris Paul. The programme, called the Mischief for Change Scholarship, aimed to provide financial assistance to students attending Historically Black Colleges and Universities (HBCUs) and Predominantly Black Institutions (PBIs) Chris Paul joined the team as a judge, helping select the recipients.

Article Title: 'We need money for midterms': Ex-RFK Jr aide alleges corruption in Trump admin
Article Text:
The former adviser also criticised the administration's delay in establishing a definition for ultra-processed foods, another major MAHA priority.

Former White House official Calley Means has alleged that a group of influential people within US President Donald Trump's administration worked to advance corporate interests at the expense of public health priorities, claiming that financial considerations also influenced key policy decisions.Means, a former adviser to Health Secretary Robert F Kennedy Jr, made the allegations during an interview on 'The Joe Rogan Experience' on Friday. He said his decision to resign from the administration stemmed from what he described as internal corruption and a group of officials working against the agenda that voters had supported."The simple reality in why I left is that there is a very concentrated group of people in the Trump administration that are antagonistic to what people voted for and are, frankly, — I think it's very clear — doing things for other reasons," Means said."Particularly in many cases to enrich their families," he added.According to Means, outgoing White House chief of staff Susie Wiles played a central role in ensuring that corporate interests influenced the administration's decisions, particularly on health-related policies. He alleged that Wiles repeatedly emphasised the need to raise money ahead of the midterm elections and prioritised contributions from powerful business groups."Susie said to me many times, ‘We need money for the midterms, Calley. We need money for the midterms,’" he said, adding that she had also told him, "I need the money from the sugar people to win the midterms."Means further claimed that Wiles had considerable control over policy decisions and that companies employing her daughter as a lobbyist received preferential treatment when seeking funding from the administration.One of the major disagreements, he said, concerned the administration's position on glyphosate, the active ingredient in Bayer's weedkiller Roundup. The Trump administration had faced criticism from Make America Healthy Again (MAHA) activists after issuing an executive order calling for an adequate supply of glyphosate-based herbicides on national security grounds.Means alleged that officials worked behind the scenes to undermine Kennedy's efforts to scrutinise the chemical. He also claimed that a Justice Department lawyer who had previously worked with a firm representing Bayer drafted an opinion urging the Supreme Court to take up the company's case and limit its liability in cancer-related lawsuits.The former adviser also criticised the administration's delay in establishing a definition for ultra-processed foods, another major MAHA priority."The amount of vitriol and lobbying on this issue, just having a simple definition out, because the food companies don't want people to know the truth," he said.Responding to the allegations, White House spokeswoman Allison Schuster told Axios that the administration had secured several victories for the MAHA agenda, including changes to dietary guidelines and efforts to remove artificial ingredients from the food supply.Trump announced on Friday that Wiles would leave her position, with Stephen Miller set to replace her as chief of staff. Kennedy, meanwhile, defended the administration's record, saying he and Trump "intend to keep fighting until the American people—not corporate influence—drive our health policies."
Article Summary: Calley Means, a former adviser to Health Secretary Robert F Kennedy Jr, made the allegations during an interview on 'The Joe Rogan Experience' on Friday. He said his decision to resign from the administration stemmed from what he described as internal corruption and officials working against the agenda that voters had supported.

Article Title: Dana White declines Trump's offer to become White House press secretary: Report
Article Text:
Trump with Dana White

President Donald Trump ’s unusual offer to appoint Ultimate Fighting Championship (UFC) chief Dana White as White House press secretary has been declined, CNN reported, citing a source familiar with the matter.Trump announced on Saturday that he had offered White the position, describing him as a “violent Fighter and Warrior” in a post on his Truth Social platform. However, despite the public appeal, White has turned down the offer, leaving Trump without a permanent chief spokesperson.“I am pleased to announce that the Great Dana White, a violent Fighter and Warrior, has been offered the job of Press Secretary of the United States,” Trump wrote.Also Read| 'Extortion at the highest level': Trump directs DOJ to investigate Democratic lawmakers The US president also asked White to bring along six UFC fighters as “assistants”, sharing their photographs in the post. He suggested that they would help defend his administration against political opponents.“We need these people to defend us against the Lunatic Left. Dana will be a Press Secretary like none other. Dana, please take the job!” Trump added.White, who is a close friend of Trump, was in London on Saturday attending a boxing event when he was asked about the announcement.He said he planned to travel to Washington and meet the president at the White House on Monday.When questioned about how he would manage the potential responsibilities alongside his existing roles in the fighting industry, White appeared taken aback before responding, “Yeah, I got a lot of jobs already.”He declined to disclose details of his conversations with Trump, adding, “I'm sure I'll have more to talk about after that.”Before the news conference, White had also shared Trump's post on Instagram, alongside an image of himself standing behind the podium in the White House briefing room, with the caption “On to the next chapter.”Also Read| ‘Dana, please take the job!’: Trump offers UFC chief White House press secy post Trump's announcement came amid a period of uncertainty within his administration. The White House has been without a permanent press secretary since Karoline Leavitt left the position at the end of August. Her successor, Katie Zacharia, lasted just five days in the role after an uncomfortable appearance before reporters.The latest development also comes after Republicans suffered major losses in the midterm elections, losing control of both chambers of Congress.
Article Summary: Dana White has turned down President Donald Trump's offer to be his White House press secretary, CNN reported. Trump announced on Saturday that he had offered White the position, describing him as a “violent Fighter and Warrior” The US president also asked White to bring along six UFC fighters as “assistants”

Article Title: NFL star Khalil Mack created a scholarship programme inspired by his No. 52 jersey; his foundation committed $270,400 to support 52 Florida students
Article Text:
PC: Bold.org

How did Mack's Florida roots inspire the No. 52 scholarship programme

How can students apply for the $270,400 Khalil Mack scholarship

What is the mission of the Khalil Mack Foundation

NFL star Khalil Mack and his wife, Brianna, have launched a scholarship programme inspired by his No. 52 jersey, with the Khalil Mack Foundation committing $270,400 to support 52 Florida students. The Khalil Mack 52 Scholars Program, announced on 1 June 2026 in partnership with the scholarship platform Bold, will award $5,200 to each of its 52 recipients. The programme is open to African-American high school seniors, undergraduates and trade school students in Florida who have a GPA of 3.0 or higher and limited financial resources. Applicants are asked to write a 400–600 word essay on a turning point in their lives. Winners are due to be announced on 15 August 2026 “I just want to spread some kind of positivity back home,” Mack said.The press release says both Mack and his wife have deep roots in Florida. Mack was born and raised in Fort Pierce, while Brianna grew up in Coral City in Miami Gardens. Bold states that their experiences gave them a personal understanding of the talent and potential found across the state, as well as the financial barriers that can keep young people from educational opportunities.According to the release, the couple is investing directly in students who demonstrate resilience, leadership and a commitment to their communities. It describes the programme as designed to help students pursue college, university and career-training opportunities while reducing the financial pressure that can accompany higher education. The initiative reflects the determination and perseverance that have defined Mack's journey, from an under-the-radar high school recruit to one of the most accomplished defensive players of his generation.The Bold scholarship page lists the eligibility requirements. Applicants must be a high school senior, undergraduate or trade school student with a GPA of 3.0 or higher. They must also live in Florida, have limited financial resources and be African-American. The Khalil Mack Foundation's scholarship page sets out the same criteria. It adds that applicants must be enrolled, or planning to enrol, in an accredited college, university or trade school. The Bold press release states that preference will be given to students with demonstrated financial need.To apply, students are asked to tell their story and explain how their experiences have shaped their commitment to education, community and their goals. The Bold listing gives the essay length as 400–600 words and the selection criteria as ambition, drive and impact. It also states the essay topic: every story has a turning point, whether a moment, a person or a season, and applicants are asked to share theirs. The application window opened on 1 June 2026. Bold lists the deadline as 1 August 2026, while the Foundation's website gives 31 July 2026. 15 August 2026 is the date for winners to be announced or notified.The Khalil Mack Foundation's website describes the organisation as committed to empowering the next generation of leaders through education, mentorship and opportunity. It says the Foundation is guided by faith and grounded in gratitude, and that it believes in paying forward the blessings that shaped its founders. The Foundation is a faith-rooted, heart-led organisation. It says the Foundation works to meet basic needs, strengthen community pride and empower the next generation, and that its mission is to invest in the communities that shaped Khalil and Brianna Mack. The Foundation's website closes with the line "I can. I will. I did. For us."Bold says it was founded in 2019 to fight student debt and is the largest independent scholarship platform in the United States. The release states that more than 10k+ donors have used the platform to create personalised scholarships, and that Bold is free for students and donors. It adds that donations are administered through the Bold Foundation, a nonprofit organisation, and that 100% of each primary donation goes directly to funding students' education. Bold founder and chief executive Dror Liebenthal is quoted in the release as saying that the programme recognises the resilience, leadership and potential of young people who are already making a difference in their communities. He also said Bold is proud to partner with the Foundation to help remove barriers to education.
Article Summary: The Khalil Mack 52 Scholars Program will award $5,200 to each of its 52 recipients. It is open to African-American high school seniors, undergraduates and trade school students in Florida who have a GPA of 3.0 or higher. Applicants are asked to write a 400–600 word essay on a turning point in their lives. Winners are due to be announced on 15 August 2026.

Article Title: Balochistan Parties call statewide shutdown in mid-November as crisis deepens in troubled province
Article Text:
(Representative image) (Photo: ANI).

Political parties in Pakistan’s Balochistan province have called a province-wide shutdown strike for November 19, to be followed by demonstrations at district headquarters. They accuse the provincial and federal governments of failing to address mounting security, political and economic concerns.The decision was taken at an all-parties conference organised by the Awami National Party (ANP) at the Quetta Press Club, according to a report by The Express Tribune cited by ANI. ANP provincial president Asghar Khan Achakzai chaired the meeting, which was attended by representatives of the National Party, Jamiat Ulema-e-Islam, Pashtunkhwa National Awami Party and several other political groups. The participants agreed to bring their joint political and democratic efforts under a coordinated movement to raise public grievances.In a joint declaration, the parties described the situation in Balochistan as alarming. They cited persistent insecurity, terrorism, extremism, armed group activities, targeted killings and kidnappings for ransom. They also raised the unresolved issue of missing persons, and highlighted the difficulties faced by transporters and passengers travelling on national highways.The parties pointed to rising unemployment and economic decline. They blamed the closure of trade and transit routes with Afghanistan and Iran for disrupting economic activity across the province. Soaring inflation, prolonged power and gas outages, petroleum levies and restrictions on the supply of essential agricultural inputs, including urea fertiliser, were also cited. According to The Express Tribune, the leaders said these issues had adversely affected agriculture, trade, industries and employment.The participating parties also criticised the provincial and federal governments, accusing them of failing to ensure public safety, maintain law and order, protect natural resources and restore economic stability.Furthermore, the parties announced a provincial-level meeting on November 26 to decide the next course of action. An all-parties conference will be held in the first week of December to take Balochistan’s concerns to the national leadership.
Article Summary: Political parties in Pakistan’s Balochistan province have called a province-wide shutdown strike for November 19. They accuse the provincial and federal governments of failing to address mounting security, political and economic concerns. The decision was taken at an all-parties conference organised by the Awami National Party (ANP)

Article Title: 'If he wishes to come’: Pakistan open to considering visa for Punjab CM Bhagwant Mann’s Lahore visit
Article Text:
पंजाब सीएम भगवंत मान

Poll Vote & Share your view Do you think Punjab Chief Minister Bhagwant Mann should visit Pakistan for the World Punjabi Conference? Yes, it would promote cultural ties. No, travel could be risky. 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

NEW DELHI: Pakistan has indicated its willingness to grant a visa to Punjab chief minister Bhagwant Mann should he wish to visit the neighbouring country for the World Punjabi Conference in Lahore on November 27, following an invitation to the event.Pakistan Foreign Office spokesperson Sajjad Haider Khan made the remarks during his weekly media briefing while responding to a question about Mann's possible visit, PTI reported."The government would consider issuing Mann a visa if he wishes to visit Pakistan. However, whether the Indian government permits him to travel is an entirely separate matter," he told reporters in Islamabad.On October 23, Mann had said that he had received an invitation to attend the World Punjabi Conference in Lahore.However, the Punjab chief minister also raised doubts over whether he would be permitted to travel to Pakistan.“Our culture is the same. Many poets from here will go there,” he remarked.Mann had also voiced his wish for all members of the Punjab legislative assembly to visit Kartarpur Sahib in Pakistan if it reopened.The corridor, which links Dera Baba Nanak in Punjab with the historic Gurdwara Darbar Sahib in Kartarpur, Pakistan, was established to facilitate Sikh pilgrims visiting the shrine associated with Guru Nanak Dev, the founder of Sikhism.It enables Indian pilgrims to visit the gurdwara without a Pakistani visa, subject to applicable arrangements.The corridor has remained closed to pilgrims travelling from the India since May 7, 2025, when India launched pre-dawn missile strikes on nine terror targets in Pakistan and Pakistan-occupied Kashmir following the Pahalgam terror attack on April 22.Last month, the Centre denied political clearance to Mann for his visit to Paris, prompting the Punjab government to challenge the decision before the Punjab and Haryana high court.The high court subsequently cleared his visit, observing that the Centre had “not explained” the political considerations it cited while refusing permission for his trip to the French capital.
Article Summary: Pakistan has indicated its willingness to grant a visa to Punjab chief minister Bhagwant Mann should he wish to visit the neighbouring country for the World Punjabi Conference in Lahore on November 27. Pakistan Foreign Office spokesperson Sajjad Haider Khan made the remarks during his weekly media briefing.

Article Title: Pakistan’s forex rises by record $ 110 million in just a week despite West Asia crisis
Article Text:
Pakistan’s central bank reported a $110 million weekly rise in foreign exchange reserves, taking total holdings to a record $26.864 billion

Pakistan’s foreign exchange reserves rose by $110 million in a week to a record $26.864 billion, according to the State Bank of Pakistan (SBP), even as the West Asia conflict continues to disrupt global energy markets and push up oil prices.In a statement on Thursday, the central bank said the country's total reserves had increased from $26.754 billion in the previous week.The rise included a $39 million increase in SBP-held reserves, while commercial banks' foreign exchange holdings also improved.The SBP said Pakistan's reserves had increased by $5 billion since the conflict began in February. Its own holdings rose from $16.568 billion in February to $21.568 billion as of October 30. The central bank said the improved reserve position had helped stabilise the exchange rate and provided exporters with confidence to repatriate their earnings without delay.However, Pakistan continues to face a substantial trade gap. Its trade deficit stood at $14.6 billion in the first four months of FY27, with imports at $26 billion against exports of $11.4 billion. Financial analysts have attributed the stability of the Pakistani rupee and the improvement in foreign exchange availability largely to rising remittances.
Article Summary: Pakistan’s foreign exchange reserves rose by $110 million in a week to a record $26.864 billion, according to the State Bank of Pakistan. The rise included a $39 million increase in SBP-held reserves. The SBP said Pakistan's reserves had increased by $5 billion since the conflict began in February.

Article Title: How deep is Pakistan's debt dependence on China? The numbers tell the story
Article Text:
China leads as external debt touches $135 billion

Poll Vote & Share your view Should Pakistan rely more on multilateral institutions for financial aid? Yes, it's safer No, seek private investors 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

Pakistan’s external debt has nearly doubled over the past decade, climbing to $135.1 billion in 2025 from $68.67 billion in 2015, according to a World Bank report cited by Dawn.The figures underline the Islamic country’s growing dependence on foreign borrowing to meet its financial needs.The debt stock comprised $107.07 billion in public and publicly guaranteed loans, $17.58 billion in private non-guaranteed debt and $10.45 billion in short-term borrowing.Of the public debt, multilateral institutions accounted for the largest share at $56.83 billion. Pakistan also owed $42.43 billion to bilateral lenders and $7.8 billion to private creditors.China remained Pakistan’s biggest individual creditor, with outstanding loans of $22.4 billion. The World Bank was next with $19.2 billion, followed by the Asian Development Bank (ADB), to which Pakistan owed $16.83 billion.The report also highlighted the difference in borrowing costs. Loans from official creditors had an average maturity of 16 years, a four-year grace period and an interest rate of 3.6%. Private credit, in contrast, came at a much steeper average interest rate of 8.6%, with a repayment period of three years and a grace period of just one year.Across the Middle East, North Africa, Afghanistan and Pakistan region, debt-service and interest ratios showed improvement.However, the region’s external debt-to-gross national income (GNI) ratio rose from 26.7% to 29.4% in 2025. This was the sharpest annual increase recorded by any region, pointing to a continued build-up of external debt.Pakistan also received some relief through fresh financing and loan extensions during the year. China extended the maturity of $2 billion in loans, while the International Monetary Fund (IMF) disbursed $2.3 billion under its Extended Fund Facility and Resilience and Sustainability Facility programmes, aimed at supporting the country’s longer-term economic stability.
Article Summary: Pakistan’s external debt has nearly doubled over the past decade, climbing to $135.1 billion in 2025 from $68.67 billion in 2015. Of the public debt, multilateral institutions accounted for the largest share at $56.83 billion. Pakistan also owed $42.43 billion to bilateral lenders and $7.8 billion to private creditors.

Article Title: 11 dead, 33 injured in devastating bus-truck collision in eastern Pakistan
Article Text:
.

At least 11 people were killed and 33 others injured after a passenger bus collided with a truck in eastern Pakistan on Thursday, police and rescue officials said.The accident occurred in Pakpattan district of Punjab province, AP reported, citing hospital official Dr Ahmad Raza. Rescue teams used cranes and other heavy machinery to pull passengers trapped inside the wreckage. The operation lasted nearly three hours, police said.Authorities declared an emergency at the hospital and called in additional doctors and medical personnel to treat the injured, Raza said.Pakistan president Asif Ali Zardari expressed grief over the deaths in a statement, shared on social media, while also extending his condolences to the bereaved families and prayed for the speedy recovery of those injured.“Extending his best wishes for the speedy recovery of the injured, he directed the relevant authorities to continue providing all possible support for medical treatment and relief operations,” the statement added.Road accidents are common in Pakistan, where poor road conditions, inadequate enforcement of traffic regulations and unsafe driving practices contribute to frequent collisions. Last month, at least 12 people were killed and around two dozen others injured after a bus collided with a van in the southwestern province of Balochistan, according to AP.
Article Summary: A bus collided with a truck in eastern Pakistan, police and rescue officials say. Rescue teams used cranes and other heavy machinery to pull passengers trapped inside the wreckage. Pakistan president Asif Ali Zardari expresses grief over the deaths. Road accidents are common in Pakistan, where poor road conditions contribute to frequent collisions.

Article Title: Where Is Bashir Zeb Baloch? Mystery mounts after BLA announces leadership change
Article Text:
BLA announces Bashir Zeb Baloch’s exit as chief, while unverified reports swirl over his whereabouts and possible death (Image credit: X posts)

NEW DELHI: Mystery shrouds the status and whereabouts of Baloch Liberation Army (BLA) Commander-in-Chief Bashir Zeb Baloch, following an announcement by the rebel group on Tuesday that he was stepping down from his post. The announcement stood in contrast to claims circulating on pro-Pakistan military social media accounts that suggest an assassination attempt or his death.Rumours across pro-Pakistan Telegram channels, citing unnamed sources, speculated that Zeb was the target of a poisoning attempt by a close confidant in Kandahar and was subsequently rushed to a military hospital.Other accounts went further, claiming he was eliminated in a Pakistani military airstrike inside Afghanistan in September — a claim that remains independently unverified.Zeb had emerged as the primary face of the BLA's major offensive, Operation Herof. Visuals released during the operation depicting him riding a motorcycle without security cover had created significant ripples across security and intelligence circles.In an official statement issued by the BLA, the group clarified the context around Zeb's departure saying: "Following the decision of the Senior Command Council in accordance with the constitution of the organization, former Commander-in-Chief of the Baloch Liberation Army, Bashir Zeb Baloch, will no longer serve as the head of the organization.""Until the selection of a new Commander-in-Chief, all administrative, military, and policy-making powers have been officially entrusted to the Senior Command Council, the highest supreme body of the BLA, while military operations across all fronts will continue without interruption," the statement from BLA said.The rebel group saidnthat during the reorganization of the BLA in 2018, the ideological and structural founder of the BLA, Ustad Aslam Baloch, had brought an end to hereditary politics and lifelong leadership, establishing the organization on the foundations of merit, transparency, and institutional principles."He set the guiding principle that no matter how influential, prominent, or high-ranking a commander may be in this movement, no individual can remain Commander-in-Chief for life. To maintain this ideological and organizational continuity, a clear and consensus-based procedure was incorporated into the BLA constitution so that, if the need ever arose, an established and peaceful constitutional pathway for a smooth leadership transition would exist. ""In accordance with this principle, a joint meeting of the highest bodies of the BLA was held on October 16, during which constitutional and organizational matters were thoroughly reviewed. During the meeting, all commanders unanimously decided in favor of leadership transition to impart fresh momentum to the organization's activities," the statement said."Our operational activities across all fronts continue without interruption. The name of the new Commander-in-Chief will be announced soon at the conclusion of the next phases," the BLA said.
Article Summary: Mystery shrouds the status and whereabouts of Baloch Liberation Army (BLA) Commander-in-Chief Bashir Zeb Baloch. Zeb had emerged as the primary face of the BLA's major offensive, Operation Herof. Unverified reports suggest an assassination attempt or his death.

Article Title: Asim Munir flags growing Hindu-Jewish ties threat to Pakistan and Muslim world, reveals Iran
Article Text: Iran's senior security official Mohsen Rezaei has claimed that Pakistan Army chief Asim Munir warned of growing ties between Hindus and Jews, alleging that the emerging partnership posed a threat to Pakistan and the wider Muslim world.In an interview with Iranian state media, Rezaei said Munir raised concerns over growing India-Israel ties during a four-nation security meeting in Tehran on October 26. The meeting was attended by Munir, Turkish intelligence chief Ibrahim Kalin, Saudi defence minister Prince Khalid bin Salman and Rezaei, who represented Iran.Rezaei also claimed that the leaders shared concerns that Israel could target other countries in the region after Iran."They spoke very strongly against Israel. Mr Khalid bin Salman said that after you (Iran), Israel would target Turkey, and then come after Saudi Arabia," Rezaei said during the interview."Mr Ibrahim Kalin, the head of Turkish intelligence, shared the same view. Mr Asim Munir also spoke about the threat posed by Israel and the emerging bond between Hindus and Jews against Muslims and even Pakistan. These remarks reflect their information and concerns about how Israel may act towards them in the future," he added.Munir has repeatedly invoked religious differences between Hindus and Muslims, describing the two communities as fundamentally distinct.Days before the Pakistan-backed Pahalgam terror attack in April 2025, Munir had spoken about the differences between Hindus and Muslims in their religion, customs, traditions, thoughts and ambitions. He had also invoked the Two-Nation Theory.While Rezaei's latest account of Munir's remarks remains unverified, the reported comments are consistent with the Pakistani army chief's earlier rhetoric.Meanwhile, India and Israel have steadily expanded cooperation across defence, intelligence, counterterrorism, trade, agriculture, water management and emerging technologies. The two countries elevated their relationship to a Special Strategic Partnership during PM Narendra Modi's visit to Israel in February 2026.Israel had also openly backed India's right to self-defence during Operation Sindoor against Pakistan in May 2025. Israeli Ambassador to India Reuven Azar had said that terrorists had nowhere to hide.In February this year, Israeli PM Benjamin Netanyahu proposed a "hexagon of alliances" involving India, Israel, Greece, Cyprus and other countries to counter what he described as radical Shia and Sunni axes.In October, Netanyahu again named India as a key partner in his plans to build alternative alliances. He also warned that Israel could face a hostile US administration after President Donald Trump leaves the White House.
Article Summary: Pakistan Army chief Asim Munir raised concerns over growing India-Israel ties during a four-nation security meeting in Tehran on October 26. Munir, Turkish intelligence chief Ibrahim Kalin, Saudi defence minister Prince Khalid bin Salman and Rezaei, who represented Iran.

Article Title: 'America taking its place': Shehbaz's rival Fazlur Rehman accuses Asim Munir of sabotaging ties with China
Article Text: Jamiat Ulema-e-Islam-Fazl (JUI-F) chief Maulana Fazlur Rehman on Monday accused Pakistan army of derailing Chinese investments under the China-Pakistan Economic Corridor ( CPEC ), alleging that the country's mineral wealth was being used to advance foreign interests and facilitate a shift towards United States.In a social media post on X, Rehman claimed that Pakistan had disappointed Beijing by halting CPEC-linked investments midway and warned that the loss of Chinese confidence could deter other countries from investing in Pakistan."You have disappointed China, you have halted their investment midway, and when China is disappointed, the rest of the world will not come to invest in your country either," he said.He alleged that the US was stepping in to fill the space left by China, claiming that American officials had acknowledged this to him."And who is taking China's place? America is taking its place. This has been admitted by the Americans themselves in front of me," he said.Rehman clarified that he was not opposed to foreign investment in Pakistan's mineral sector, saying the country urgently needed international capital, development projects and economic opportunities."We do not disagree with the principle of investment from around the world here.Multinational companies come, they invest; America is not immune to this, Russia is not immune, China is not immune, Britain and France are not immune," he said."And who is taking China's place? America is taking its place. This has been admitted by the Americans themselves in front of me, and our esteemed elders here have taken those beautiful, beautiful stones to their offices and presented them, and the ambassador they have here at the time has also said it in her interview," he added.The JUI-F chief also alleged that politicians backed by the military establishment prioritised their personal interests and the demands of their patrons over Pakistan's economic well-being."These Pakistani politicians - whose priorities I know - in all such matters, they first determine their own share, and only then do they think about the country," he said.Fazlur Rehman also questioned the imposition of governor's rule and the declaration of an emergency in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, alleging that the measures were linked to concerns over the region's mineral reserves."On what grounds? Terrorism? The provincial government is aligned with the narrative of terrorism; it is the federation that is not providing support for that narrative," he said.He further alleged that the focus on terrorism had subsequently disappeared from the debate, while discussions surrounding mineral reserves had also been dropped."As soon as governor's rule was imposed and as soon as the emergency was declared, the topic of terrorism simply vanished, and from their side, the discussion of mineral reserves was dropped," he said.His remarks come amid Pakistan's efforts to attract foreign investment into its mineral sector, particularly in resource-rich regions such as Balochistan and Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.CPEC, a flagship component of China's Belt and Road Initiative, includes infrastructure, energy and industrial development projects. The initiative has faced challenges over the years, including security threats, delays and concerns over the safety of Chinese personnel and investments.
Article Summary: Jamiat Ulema-e-Islam-Fazl (JUI-F) chief Maulana Fazlur Rehman accused Pakistan army of derailing Chinese investments under the China-Pakistan Economic Corridor ( CPEC) He alleged that the country's mineral wealth was being used to advance foreign interests and facilitate a shift towards United States.

Article Title: Pakistan's confidence crisis: Government officials plan to move families abroad for secure future
Article Text:
Shehbaz Sharif-led Pakistan govt faces confidence crisis as officials plan to move families abroad.

Pakistan is facing questions over the confidence of its own governing establishment, with defence minister Khawaja Asif alleging that some officials holding important positions in the country are planning to settle abroad, including in Portugal and other Western nations.The reported plans have drawn attention to a wider contradiction for the nation grappled with the economic crisis.While the government expects citizens to remain patient amid the country's difficulties, some people within the administration are said to be looking at opportunities and a more secure future overseas for themselves and their families, reported Greek City Times.The issue goes beyond officials moving abroad after retirement as it also raises questions about whether their families are already preparing to build lives elsewhere through overseas education, residency and eventual settlement.If the children of officials study and settle abroad, their families could become less dependent on Pakistan's institutions, even as those officials continue to hold positions of authority at home.The issue of family members studying abroad is also covered in Pakistan's official disclosure requirements. The Establishment Division's asset declaration form asks government officials to provide details of their children's education, including whether they are studying in Pakistan or overseas.It also seeks information about relevant family assets and expenditure.These requirements do not establish how many officials have sent their children abroad or whether they intend to settle overseas. However, they show that such financial arrangements are considered relevant to official disclosure and scrutiny.The reported plans come against the backdrop of a wider migration trend involving Pakistan's educated and professional workforce.In October, overseas Pakistanis minister Chaudhry Salik Hussain told the National Assembly that more than 1.8 million highly educated and professional people had left Pakistan over the previous three years, Pakistan Today reported.The people who moved abroad included doctors, information technology professionals, engineers, academics and skilled workers from several other sectors. Their departure raises concerns about the country's ability to retain experienced professionals across essential industries.The figures cited by the minister underline the scale of the movement of skilled workers out of Pakistan at a time of unprecendented economic crisis.
Article Summary: Pakistan facing confidence crisis as officials plan to move families abroad. Defence minister Khawaja Asif alleges some officials are planning to settle abroad, including in Portugal and other Western nations. Issue goes beyond officials moving abroad after retirement as it also raises questions about whether their families are already preparing to build lives elsewhere.

Article Title: Pakistan gas crisis: Families return to firewood as LPG prices soar ahead of winter
Article Text:
File photo: Pakistan's fuel crisis forces families back to firewood and coal

With natural gas available for barely six hours a day and LPG prices soaring, families in Pakistan’s Rawalpindi are returning to firewood, coal and kerosene to keep their kitchens running as winter approaches.According to a report by The Express Tribune, households are increasingly relying on cheaper alternatives such as discarded furniture wood and sawdust. Residents are also facing steep increases in the cost of LPG cylinders, with a new domestic cylinder selling for PKR13,500 (approx Rs 4644), compared with PKR10,000 (approx Rs 3440) earlier. Refill charges have risen from PKR3,000 (approx Rs 1032) to PKR5,000 (approx Rs 1720), while commercial cylinder refills have nearly doubled to PKR25,000 (approx Rs 8600).The cost of firewood and coal has also climbed. Dry firewood is selling for PKR1,500 (approx Rs 516) to PKR1,800 (approx Rs 619) per maund, while ordinary firewood costs PKR1,300 (approx 447) to PKR1,400 (approx Rs 482). Coal is priced between PKR800 (approx Rs 275) and PKR1,000 (approx Rs 344) per maund, depending on quality, and sawdust costs around PKR700 (approx Rs 240) per maund.Muhammad Faizan, a furniture factory owner, told The Express Tribune that waste wood previously dumped near Nullah Lai was now being collected by residents for cooking.Shehzad Manzoor Kiyani, divisional president of the All-Pakistan Clerks Association, said inflation and unreliable gas supplies had forced government employees to return to firewood and coal. He said households were spending PKR10,000 (approx Rs 3440) to PKR12,000 (approx Rs 4127) a month on LPG.The household crisis comes as Pakistan’s LPG supply faces further pressure. The Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority (Ogra) has raised the official LPG price for November to PKR 294,075 (approx Rs 1,01,138) per tonne, from PKR 279,341 (approx Rs 96,084) in October. The price of an 11.8-kg domestic cylinder has consequently risen by PKR 173 (approx Rs 59) to PKR 3,470 (approx Rs 1,194), taking the official retail rate to PKR 294 (approx Rs 101) per kg.But LPG is reportedly selling for as much as PKR 630 (approx Rs 217) per kg in the open market, while company-operated franchises are charging up to PKR 400 (approx Rs 138) per kg. Ogra said the increase followed a 6.47% rise in Saudi Aramco’s contract price, despite a marginal 0.12% decline in the average dollar exchange rate.LPG Distributors Association of Pakistan chairman Irfan Khokhar said the situation was serious because of the closure of the Iran border. He claimed that at least 70% of Pakistan’s LPG was imported from Iran, with the remaining 30% produced locally, and urged the government to curb market manipulation.Meanwhile, the Pakistan LPG Marketers Association has threatened to shut down businesses from November 16 if the government sidelines the private sector under its proposed LPG policy. Association chairman Ali Haider said the government should retain the sector’s deregulated structure, arguing that the private sector played a major role in imports.Haider said that of around 1.3 million tonnes of LPG consumed, approximately 225,000 tonnes were imported from the Gulf, largely by private companies. In a letter to petroleum minister Ali Pervaiz Malik, the association said the draft policy sent to the prime minister had been prepared without private-sector input and called for complete deregulation of the LPG sector.The association also criticised the petroleum development levy of Rs4,669 per tonne on locally produced LPG under the 2016 policy. The levy was intended to help state-owned entities, including Pakistan State Oil, Parco and Sui Southern Gas Company, import LPG during winter and emergencies. Haider alleged that despite billions of rupees being collected through the levy, these entities had failed to import supplies during the current shortage.
Article Summary: Natural gas available for barely six hours a day in Rawalpindi. Families are increasingly relying on cheaper alternatives such as discarded furniture wood and sawdust. Residents are also facing steep increases in the cost of LPG cylinders, with a new domestic cylinder selling for PKR13,500 (approx Rs 4644)

Article Title: India should arm Afghan Taliban against Pakistan: Sushant Sareen
Article Text:
-

India should consider formally recognising the Taliban government in Afghanistan and providing it with military assistance to counter Pakistan, strategic affairs analyst Sushant Sareen has argued, calling for a rethink of New Delhi’s approach to its western neighbourhood.Speaking on Faultline with Ananya Dasgupta on Times Axis, Sareen said India should not allow international consensus to dictate its Afghanistan policy. He argued that if Pakistan was using military force to pressure the Taliban, India should consider helping the Afghan regime defend itself.“If the Afghan Taliban are going to be bullied by the Pakistanis… then maybe we should help them militarily,” Sareen said. “So that they can also hit back.”He went beyond making a general case for military assistance, suggesting that India consider supplying Afghanistan with anti-drone systems, drone technology and missile capabilities.“If you can give them some anti-drone systems to the Afghans, if you can give them maybe some drone technology, which will help them fight back, maybe give them some missile systems or, you know, long-range rocket systems,” Sareen said.“Why not? I think we should consider it so that at least the Pakistanis cannot, you know, bully somebody into submission,” he added, arguing that India needed to be more willing to take risks if it wanted to project power internationally.Sareen’s argument comes against the backdrop of growing tensions between Pakistan and the Taliban, once backed by Islamabad but now increasingly unwilling to follow its instructions. The conflict has exposed the limits of Pakistan’s long-standing effort to exercise strategic influence over Afghanistan.Sareen said India should also reconsider its refusal to formally recognise the Taliban government, which came to power in 2021. He argued that recognition need not mean approval of the regime’s ideology or policies.“Recognition does not mean endorsement,” he said, pointing out that countries maintain diplomatic relations with governments whose actions they do not necessarily agree with.According to Sareen, the Taliban are the de facto rulers of Afghanistan and India already has a degree of engagement with them. He questioned why New Delhi should continue to hold back from formal recognition simply because other countries have not changed their position.Sareen said New Delhi should make its own assessment of what serves Indian interests, rather than remain constrained by concerns about how other countries might react.“The world doesn't ask us for our opinions before they start doing things,” he said.Sareen believes Pakistan’s Afghan strategy has backfired. Islamabad once viewed the Taliban as a means of securing influence in Afghanistan, but the relationship has turned adversarial as the Taliban has asserted its own interests.Explaining the mistake in Pakistan’s calculations, Sareen said Islamabad had mistaken a temporary alliance with sections of the Afghan population for lasting control.“You can rent an Afghan, you can't buy him,” he said, adding that the Afghans acted in Pakistan’s interests only as long as it suited them. Once they gained greater agency, they began pursuing their own priorities.Pakistan accuses the Taliban of providing sanctuary to the Tehreek-e-Taliban Pakistan (TTP), whose attacks have targeted the Pakistani state. The Taliban, in turn, has resisted pressure from Islamabad and accused Pakistan of backing groups opposed to its rule.Sareen also discussed Pakistan’s interest in the Wakhan Corridor, a narrow strip of Afghan territory that could provide direct connectivity to Central Asia. He said Pakistan appeared to see control of the corridor as a way to gain strategic leverage over the Taliban, but warned that such a move could invite retaliation.For India, Sareen argued, the question is whether the deteriorating relationship between Pakistan and the Taliban creates an opportunity to protect its own strategic interests. He urged New Delhi to consider both diplomatic recognition and military assistance, while acknowledging that a more assertive role would carry risks.His proposal raises a difficult question for Indian policymakers: could a former Pakistani ally now become a strategic counterweight to Islamabad — and is New Delhi prepared to act on that possibility?
Article Summary: India should not allow international consensus to dictate its Afghanistan policy, says Sushant Sareen. He argues that if Pakistan was using military force to pressure the Taliban, India should consider helping the Afghan regime defend itself. He suggests that India consider supplying Afghanistan with anti-drone systems, drone technology and missile capabilities.

Article Title: ‘Koi sharam hoti hai': Pak lawmaker mocks Khawaja Asif after Munir’s Iran visit
Article Text:
Fazl then turned Asif’s own words against him, repeating a phrase the defence minister had previously used to taunt PTI

Jamiat Ulema-e-Islam-Fazl (JUI-F) chief Maulana Fazlur Rehman took a jibe at Pakistan defence minister Khawaja Asif over Field Marshal Asim Munir’s participation in a high-level regional security meeting in Iran, questioning why the defence minister was absent from the talks.According to a report by Dawn, Fazl raised the issue during his address to the National Assembly on Wednesday, referring to a meeting in Tehran attended by Munir and Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi, alongside senior officials from Iran, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye.“A defence pact is taking shape in Iran, a meeting is under way (there), and the defence minister is sitting here,” Fazl said, drawing laughter and desk-thumping in the House. Pointing to Naqvi’s presence at the meeting, he asked: “The interior minister is required there as well?”Fazl then turned Asif’s own words against him, repeating a phrase the defence minister had previously used to taunt Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI).“There is your respect and stature — koi sharam hoti hai, koi haya hoti hai (have some shame, show some modesty),” he said, breaking into laughter.Responding in the National Assembly on Thursday, Asif denied that a defence pact was being negotiated in Tehran. He said the discussions had nothing to do with Pakistan’s defence or any related matter and argued that Munir had assumed a role focused on maintaining peace and dialogue following last year’s military conflict with India.The meeting brought together Munir, Naqvi, Saudi Defence Minister Prince Khalid bin Salman and Turkish intelligence chief Ibrahim Kalin, alongside senior Iranian officials, to discuss regional security and cooperation.A joint statement issued after the talks said the participants had agreed to continue their dialogue to strengthen cooperation among the four regional countries, particularly on peace and security.Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian also called for greater regional unity, saying closer cooperation among Muslim nations would help address shared challenges and resist external pressure.
Article Summary: Jamiat Ulema-e-Islam-Fazl (JUI-F) chief Maulana Fazlur Rehman took a jibe at Pakistan defence minister Khawaja Asif over Field Marshal Asim Munir’s participation in a high-level regional security meeting in Iran.

Article Title: Pakistan gas bowser explodes after truck collision, killing 2 and damaging 6 vehicles
Article Text:
Photo for representative purpose only (File)

At least two people were killed and five others critically injured after a gas bowser collided with another heavy vehicle and exploded in Pakistan's southern Sindh province on Wednesday, police said.The accident occurred on the National Highway near Rohri Interchange in Sukkur district. Preliminary reports suggest the gas bowser, which was carrying fuel under pressure, collided at high speed with a heavy trailer.The impact damaged the bowser's tank, triggering a powerful explosion and a fire that spread to nearby vehicles, Xinhua News Agency reported.Police said the two people killed were the driver and cleaner of the gas bowser. Both died at the scene after being caught in the explosion.Rescue teams and emergency services rushed to the site after receiving reports of the blast. The five injured people, who suffered serious burns and other injuries, were taken to a nearby hospital in Sukkur for treatment. Several remained in critical condition, medical personnel said.The explosion and subsequent fire also damaged or destroyed six other vehicles, including two fuel tankers, three heavy cargo trailers and a commercial Mazda truck.Police temporarily halted traffic on the National Highway and cordoned off the area around Rohri Interchange to allow firefighters and rescue teams to operate safely.Authorities began clearing the burnt wreckage and launched an investigation to establish the exact circumstances of the collision.
Article Summary: Gas bowser collided with another heavy vehicle and exploded in Pakistan's southern Sindh province. Police said the two people killed were the driver and cleaner of the gas bowser. Five injured people, who suffered serious burns and other injuries, were taken to a nearby hospital in Sukkur.
